title: Rows a Cleanup Delete Would Remove
statement: The grader for this question can only run SELECT statements, never a real write. Suppose we were about to run `DELETE FROM orders WHERE status = 'cancelled' AND amount < 100;` as a cleanup job. Write a SELECT that returns exactly the rows (all columns: `id, customer_id, status, amount`) that this DELETE would remove, ordered by id ascending - i.e. translate the DELETE's WHERE-clause logic into a SELECT instead of running the write.
starter_code:
SELECT id, customer_id, status, amount
FROM orders
WHERE -- TODO: same condition as the hypothetical DELETE's WHERE clause
ORDER BY id ASC;
hints: The rows a DELETE removes are exactly the rows its WHERE clause matches - a SELECT with the same WHERE clause shows you those rows without deleting anything
Order id 3 is cancelled but its amount (150) is not less than 100, so it should NOT appear in the result
